# s342 — affected.py selects from a map recorded at an ancestor commit

In a new worktree, `python3 tests/affected.py --run` selects tests from a sibling worktree's map recorded at an ancestor of HEAD, diffing the working tree against the map's commit, instead of asking for the full suite.

**Findings:** s337 relay 2026-10-16, later note 2: affected.py --run is unusable in a new worktree because a sibling map is borrowed only at the same HEAD, and a full discover ran past 600 s under load · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-17** — Verified: a worktree with no map of its own borrows a clean sibling map recorded at HEAD or at its nearest ancestor, diffs the working tree against that commit, and names the map and commit on stderr. Gate PASS; full suite 2333 OK (skipped=1). The owner decides whether to guard against a map recorded from a dirty tree that was committed later.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** recording or refreshing a map automatically (for example from a git hook or on `done`); borrowing a map recorded at a commit that is not an ancestor of HEAD; changing what a map records or the map format; changing the rule that the full discover runs once before done.

## Why

The s337 relay (2026-10-16, later note 2) found `affected.py --run` unusable in its new worktree. A worktree has no map of its own, and `sibling_map` (`tests/affected.py:159`) borrows one only when it was recorded at exactly the worktree's HEAD. Main's map rarely is: commits that change no code, such as filings, notes and `slicer done`, move main's HEAD without anyone rerunning the full discover there. Today main's map (`.venv/affected-map.json`) records `6a71fe3`, the s337 merge, while main is at `32f421c`. Main has had three commits since then, the s320 merge among them, so a worktree cut now borrows nothing. The fallback is a full discover. Under the load of two parallel relays that ran past the 600 s foreground limit, so implementers skip the selection step AGENTS.md asks for.

A map recorded at an ancestor commit A still describes every line that has not changed since A. `git diff -U0 A` gives the working tree's changes against A, with line numbers on A's side, which is what `parse_unified` already reads for `git diff -U0 HEAD`. Selecting from the map at A with that diff is as sound as today's same-HEAD selection: a test is selected when it ran a changed line or read a changed file since A.

Scores: importance 2 because the fast loop is the documented way to iterate and it fails in every new worktree; urgency 2 because every relay in parallel worktrees hits it; effort 1 and size S because the change is one ancestor test and one diff base in `select` and `sibling_map`. Tree slicer, pass v1.13. Discovered from s337.

## Files

- `tests/affected.py`: `select`, `sibling_map`, `working_tree_lines` (take the diff base as a parameter, defaulting to `HEAD`), the module docstring, and the stderr line that names the borrowed map.
- `tests/test_affected.py` (or wherever `sibling_map` is tested now).
- `AGENTS.md` (Commands: "a map that another worktree of the repository recorded for the same HEAD") and `CHANGELOG.md` if it records test tooling.

## Failing tests

- `test_SiblingMap_RecordedAtAncestor_IsBorrowed`: a fixture repo with two worktrees; the map is recorded in one at commit A; the other is at a descendant B. `sibling_map(B)` returns that map, and `select` diffs against A.
- `test_Select_AncestorMap_SelectsTestsForLinesChangedSinceRecorded`: a line changed between A and B, and committed, selects the test that ran it, with no uncommitted change at all.
- `test_SiblingMap_RecordedAtNonAncestor_IsPassedOver`: a map at a commit on another branch is not borrowed, and the run asks for the full suite as today.
- `test_SiblingMap_SameHead_StillPreferred`: when maps at HEAD and at an older ancestor both exist, the one at HEAD is used.
- The existing tests for a dirty sibling (uncommitted changes under `src/` or `tests/`) still pass it over.

## Implement

1. Write the failing tests against fixture repos and watch them go red.
2. In `sibling_map`, accept a candidate whose recorded SHA equals HEAD or is an ancestor of HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor RECORDED HEAD`, read only, in the fixture or checkout). Prefer an exact match; otherwise take the nearest ancestor (fewest commits from it to HEAD, `git rev-list --count RECORDED..HEAD`). Return the recorded SHA with the path.
3. In `select`, when the borrowed map's SHA is an ancestor, compute the changed lines with `git diff -U0 RECORDED --`, plus untracked files as today, and say on stderr which commit it diffs against. A worktree's own map at a different HEAD still asks for the full suite: refresh it there. Only borrowing gains the ancestor rule.
4. Mutation-check: making the ancestor test always true must turn the non-ancestor test red.

## Check

- `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full discover. `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- In a new worktree cut from main with main's map at an older ancestor: `python3 tests/affected.py --run` names the borrowed map and its commit, and runs a selection.
